edits.old: Insufficient disk capacity can break backups or restores. A standalone backup blockstore can go offline when full; restoring compressed snapshots also requires space for both the archive and extracted database files. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Insufficient disk capacity can break backups or restores. A blockstore that cannot store new blocks crashes, which blocks backups. Restoring a compressed snapshot requires sufficient space on the target host for both the compressed snapshot and its extracted database files. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/backup-restore-failures.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/ops-manager/current/tutorial/configure-block-size.md ; https://docs.opsmanager.mongodb.com/v4.0/tutorial/nav/restore-overview/

evidence.quote: If the target host does not have enough storage for the snapshot files and restored database, the restore fails.
Blockstores that can't store new blocks crash. This blocks backups. Clear space from disk to return the blockstore to working order.
Choosing compressed snapshots results in faster delivery, but requires sufficient space on the target host for both the compressed snapshot and its extracted database files.
